A.explanation: Too small by about 12 orders of magnitude. A picoampere current would transfer only about $10^8$ electrons in 24 hours, not $6.0 \times 10^{23}$.

B.explanation: Total charge $Q = Ne \approx 9.6 \times 10^4 \text{ C}$ divided by $86400 \text{ s}$ gives about $1.1 \text{ A}$.

C.explanation: About 60 times too large. It results if the 24 hours is converted to 1440 minutes instead of $86400 \text{ s}$ when using $I = Q/t$.

D.explanation: About 3600 times too large. It results if time is left as 24 hours instead of converting to seconds, giving $Q/24 \approx 4000 \text{ A}$.

hints: Notice the count is $6.0 \times 10^{23}$ free electrons passing in 24 hours, so you need the total charge carried by $N$ electrons of charge $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
Connect charge to average current with $I = Q/t$ where $Q = Ne$, so both $N$ and the time interval matter.
Convert the 24 hours into seconds with $24 \times 3600 = 86400 \text{ s}$ before dividing, then compare the size of the result in $\text{A}$ with the pA, A and kA options.
walkthrough: Convert the time to SI units: $t = 24 \text{ hours} = 24 \times 60 \times 60 = 86400 \text{ s}$, because current is charge per second.
State the charge carried by the electrons: $Q = Ne$, with $N = 6.0 \times 10^{23}$ and $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
Substitute to find total charge: $Q = (6.0 \times 10^{23})(1.60 \times 10^{-19}) = 9.6 \times 10^4 \text{ C}$.
Check units and size: $\text{C s}^{-1} = \text{A}$, and about $1 \text{ A}$ is sensible for this large electron flow. This is option B.
